描述_ZN: Fan of "Landscape Scenery and Calligraphy of the Imperial Wenjinge Composition", Qing dynasty, painted and calligraphed by Dong Ge, 17.2 cm long and 53 cm wide.　　The fan bone is black hardwood.　　One side of the fan is made of plain paper and painted with a small landscape scene in color. Inscription: "Respectfully painted by Dong Ge", with a white seal of "Ge" and a vermilion seal of "Ge".　　The landscape scene is dominated by grass-green tones, full of poetry and vitality. The painting is characterized by the "Four Kings" brushwork and ink that were prevalent in the early Qing Dynasty, and the composition is based on the method of panning and distancing with a wide field of view, with heavy mountains in the distance and pine trees in the shade, and a flat lake with blue water and lotus blossoms in the near scene. The pavilions and pavilions, bridges and pavilions in the water and mountain pass are interspersed and hidden, just like a fairyland on earth, which has the aesthetic interest of the literati's painting of indifference and seclusion. There are many scenes in the picture, but they are sparse and dense, and the heights are staggered, so that they are lively and interesting in a rigorous chapter. The mossy dots on the mountains and rocks are mostly horizontal dots with a side-sharp, recumbent brush, which gives the rocks a hard texture without losing the lush and deep charm of the mountains, representing the typical style of Dong Grant's small green landscapes.　　The other side is clay gold paper, writing the imperial "Wenjinge Song".
